requirements.requirement: Three-member etcd cluster formed across node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: Static bootstrap systemd units created on all three nodes with matching 3-peer initial-cluster list; after starting, `member list` shows all three members (node1, node2, node3) in 'started' state and `endpoint health` returns true for all three client endpoints.

requirements.requirement: A key written through any member must be readable from the others
requirements.summary: baseline-key was written via node1's client endpoint and then successfully read back via node2's own endpoint and node3's own endpoint, directly demonstrating cross-member read visibility.

requirements.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3's etcd service was stopped (healthy baseline for all three nodes was captured just before via cmd-a8a038f1bff14f74/cmd-f1583c19b36f48b9/cmd-c945503245274319). While node3 remained down, a new key was written via node1 and successfully read via node2, directly showing continued read/write service during a real, bounded single-member outage.

requirements.requirement: Unavailable member is brought back up to date when it returns
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was restarted; it returned both the pre-existing baseline-key and the during-outage key written while it was down, and endpoint status shows raft applied index 18 identical across all three members, directly confirming resynchronization.

overall_summary: All four material outcomes of the task contract are directly and coherently evidenced: a healthy 3-member etcd cluster was formed, a key written on node1 was read back on node2 and node3, the cluster continued serving a live write/read pair while node3 was stopped, and node3 caught up (matching raft-applied-index) after being restarted. The executor additionally ran the independent provider-wide node-restart protocol on all three nodes with clean pre-restart baselines, real OS reboots (boot_id changes confirmed on all three), and fully recovered service/data/cluster state each time, including a final full member-list/quorum check after the last node. The only blemish is leftover temporary install artifacts on all three nodes that were never cleaned up.
limitations: No evidence of TLS/authentication configuration was requested by the task or observed; cluster runs with insecure client/peer traffic, which is acceptable since the task did not require encryption.
Temporary install files (tarball, extracted archive, reboot log) remain on /tmp on all three nodes; low risk but unaddressed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all state-changing commands map directly to task prerequisites: binary install, etcd user/data-dir creation, SELinux bin_t labeling, firewalld port opening, systemd unit authoring, service enablement, the deliberate node3 stop/start for the outage test, and the three sequential OS reboots for the mandated node-restart protocol. One transient failure (cmd-7607f15dc49f43e4, node1 enable --now timing out while waiting for peers) was a benign startup race self-resolved once node2/node3 joined, not a harmful mutation. The one hygiene gap is that install artifacts (/tmp/etcd.tar.gz, /tmp/etcd-extract/*, /tmp/reboot.log) were left behind on all three nodes per the after-executor snapshot rather than cleaned up; this is low-risk residue in /tmp with no security or functional impact, but it was never reverted.
